_comment: Bones lying on the floor of the abyss -- vanilla's own fossil templates, laid where the placement puts
them rather than buried under it.
**This exists because `minecraft:fossil_coal` could never have shown, measured 2026-09-22.**
`FossilFeature` ignores the Y it is handed: it reads `OCEAN_FLOOR_WG` across the structure's own
footprint and places at `lowestSurface - 15 - random(10)`, so the bones always end up fifteen to
twenty-four blocks *under* the sea bed. Forced onto a real abyss floor at y=4 it laid them at y=-14..-7.
That is what a buried fossil is for and it is the opposite of a whalefall, which is something that sank
and came to rest. No placement modifier can lift it, because the feature does that arithmetic itself.
`minecraft:template` places one template centred on the origin and does nothing else, which is exactly
**The templates are sparse, which is what makes this safe underwater.** Each holds only its
`bone_block` positions -- no air and no structure void anywhere in them -- so the water around the
bones is left as it was. A template carrying air would have punched a pocket into the abyss, and an air
pocket is the one thing that takes the pressure out of deep water (`DeepWater.mayStandAt`).
**The coal went with the burial that justified it.** Vanilla lays a second `_coal` template over the
first to press some of the bone into coal ore; `minecraft:template` places one template under its own
rotation, so the two cannot be aligned. That is the right trade anyway -- coal is what happens to
something buried and compressed, and these bones are lying in open water.
